tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Sequences of BMAP-peptides and analogues
footnotes: Peptides were synthesized by the solid phase method using Fmoc-chemistry. Italicized sequences correspond to the hydrophobic C-terminal region of BMAP-peptides. Modified residues in the sequence of mBMAP-28 are underlined.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: Antibacterial activity of BMAP-peptides against E. faecium, S. agalactiae and S. marcescens
footnotes: MIC was defined as the lowest concentration of peptide preventing visible bacterial growth after incubation for 18h at 37°C. All the strains were grown in Mueller–Hinton broth. Results were determined with 1–2×105CFU/ml and are the mean of at least four independent experiments.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: Antiviral activity of BMAP-28 against human herpes simplex virus type 1
footnotes: Confluent Vero76 cells were incubated with BMAP-28 for 30min at 37°C, then washed and resuspended in growth medium. Cell survival was determined by measuring the uptake of neutral red after incubation for 48h at 37°C.

Cells were incubated with peptide and viral particles (104 TCDI50) for 30min at 37°C, then washed and resuspended in growth medium. Cell protection was determined by measuring the uptake of neutral red after 48h incubation at 37°C.
Quantification of HSV-1 inhibition was performed by virus yield inhibition assay, as described in Section 2. The results are the mean of two independent experiments performed in triplicate.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: In vitro susceptibility of the bacterial strains used in peritonitis animal model to BMAP peptides

tables.label: Table 5
tables.caption: Protective effect of BMAP-27 and -28 against E. coli, P. aeruginosa and S. aureus in an acute peritonitis mouse model
footnotes: Dose of peptide administered i.p. in a single injection after intraperitoneal bacterial challenge.
